READING PASSAGE 2
You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14-26, which are based on Reading
Passage 2 on pages 6 and 7.
Dark Chocolate’s Health-giving Benefits
A Dark chocolate might be good for our health thanks to the microbes that live in
our gut. New research suggests that beneficial bacteria that reside toward the
end of our digestive tract ferment both the antioxidants’ and the fiber in cocoa.
In their deep-gut chemistry these microbes create anti-inflammatory™
compounds that have been linked to cardiovascular and other benefits from
dark chocolate consumption. Other new research helps explain how some of
cocoa’s widespread health benefits, such as improving vascular function, may
be linked, and good for even the young and the healthy.
B_ Previous research suggested that cocoa components could be fermented, or
chemically changed, to generate beneficial compounds. Daily consumption of
dark chocolate or cocoa lowered people’s blood pressure, according to a 2012
review of 20 different studies. John Finley, a professor of food sciences at
Louisiana State University in the US, and his students took the work a step
further to see what else the body might be getting from this common treat -
and how. To follow cocoa through its digestive journey, they created a lab-built
gut, and discovered that microbes feasted on what was left of the cocoa after its
passage through the simulated digestive system. They fermented these
compounds, called flavonols, into smaller anti-inflammatory chemicals that
could be absorbed into the bloodstream.
C This simulated bodily process seems plausible from both a biological and
chemical standpoint, says Telmo Pereira of the Department of
Cardiopneumology at the Superior College of Health Technology in Portugal.
The next step, of course, will be more testing and looking for this
transformation in humans, he notes. As Grace Farhat, a researcher in the
Department of Dietetics, Nutrition and Biological Sciences at Queen Margaret
University in Edinburgh, points out, we can’t be entirely sure that each
person’s gut will undertake the same fermentation processes. The composition
of bacteria will vary in different individuals,’ she says. This will mean certain
individuals may derive more benefits than others.’
D_ These new findings, however, could help explain why dark chocolate improves
vascular function and cardiovascular health in general. Other recent research
has found that regular, moderate consumption of dark chocolate offers benefits
even for the young and healthy. Pereira and colleagues found that healthy
young adults who ate eight grams — about one small square — of 70 percent
cocoa chocolate each day for a month had ‘an obvious improvement’ in
vascular function compared to a control group. Those eating the extra
chocolate saw their blood flow increasing, on average, from 14 percent to 23
percent. The findings were published earlier this year and could have
* antioxidants: substances that prevent harmful chemical reactions
** anti-inflammatory: reducing or preventing a condition in which a part of the body becomes red, swollen and/or
painful

substantial implications for health on a broader population scale. ‘Tf
consuming dark chocolate in moderate quantities has the ability to decrease
the risk of heart disease, it could have a role to play in reducing medical costs
as well,’ Farhat says.
Of course, ‘chocolate is not a substitute for prescribed medications’, Pereira
notes. He suggests cocoa might work best for people who fall in the middle of
the bell curve for cardiovascular health. If you have a patient with severely
impaired vascular function, you cannot expect benefits from chocolate,’ he
says. And likewise, those who are already exceedingly healthy might not see
much of a boost from extra cocoa. But both he and Finley suggest that cocoa
could help in the effort to prevent heart disease. ‘Dark chocolate could well be a
preventative nutritional supplement to consider,’ Pereira says. ‘Or a
preventative snack.’
Not all chocolate is created equal, however. Dark chocolate gets all the good
publicity because it has relatively lower added sugar and fats than milk
chocolate. The benefits come from cocoa,’ Pereira notes — thus, ‘chocolates with
the highest proportion of cocoa are better.’ Even when it comes to pure cocoa,
which can be used for a hot beverage or added as a topping, he acknowledges
that no one knows the ideal amount. Even the darkest of the dark chocolates
‘must be consumed in moderation to avoid weight gain’, he notes. Finley and
his team went straight for the pure, unsweetened cocoa to test its impact on
gut microbes. Nevertheless, each type produced slightly different results. The
researchers sent three types of cocoa down the lab-rigged digestive path: lightly
processed, moderately processed and Dutch-processed. The more mildly
treated the cocoa, the more it produced beneficial compounds in these
experiments. Farhat also noted that likewise some brands of dark chocolate
‘are low in antioxidants due to the methods of manufacturing’.
With the high levels of antioxidants, cocoa might also be good for the gut itself.
It appears that if you were consuming some cocoas, it would actually stimulate
the production of healthier microbes in the colon,’ Finley says. Additionally, the
microbes broke down the undigested fiber in the cocoa. The bottom line is that
now I put cocoa on my oatmeal,’ Finley says. Although his wife dismisses the
non-traditional topping as a bit weird, Finley has science on his side for his
breakfast combo: The anti-inflammatory compounds combined with dietary
fiber is a synergistic effect - one and one makes three’ in this case, he says.
And combining cocoa with additional sources of dietary fiber might boost the
effect even more. As Finley suggests, ‘maybe chocolate-covered black beans?’

Which paragraph contains the following information?
Write the correct letter, A-G, in boxes 14-18 on your answer sheet.
14 a reference to the different kinds of cocoa used to produce chocolate
15 an explanation regarding chemicals produced from digesting cocoa which reduce
inflammation
